text: A rocket flies by throwing mass backwards really fast — and physics pushes it forwards.
The engine burns fuel and oxygen, turning them into hot gas that fires out of the nozzle.
Every bit of gas shoved down is an equal push up on the rocket — Newton's third law.
That's why it works in empty space: it never needs air to push against, only its own fuel.
Thrust beats gravity, the rocket gets lighter as fuel burns, and it keeps accelerating upward.
